title: From the lab to the gallery: import or publish?
objective: Designers see that a lesson made in the lab reaches people one of two ways: Import lesson puts it on screen in minutes but only in one browser and only until that browser is cleared, while publishing it to the gallery (add-lesson, push, tests, deploy) takes most of an hour and then lasts for everyone, unless a test fails.

recommended.why: A swimlane puts every step in the place where it happens (the lab, your computer, one browser, the repository, GitHub Actions, the site), so the two ways split visibly after Export lesson: one stays inside a browser, the other travels through the repository to the site.

alternative.why: The swimlane shows where the lesson goes; a Gantt timeline shows how long each way takes. Does seeing the 40-minute test run make the trade (quick and private, or slow and for everyone) clearer than the picture of where it lives?

assumptions: Minutes are illustrative: describing, drafting and generating take a few minutes; the test run takes about 40 minutes when a lesson changes, because the whole gallery is rebuilt and verified
Import lesson stores the lesson in the browser's own storage (localStorage) on that device; nothing is uploaded, and clearing the browser's site data erases it
Publishing means running npm run add-lesson on the exported file, committing and pushing; the test workflow runs, and the pages workflow deploys only after a green run
A failing test publishes nothing: the site keeps its last good version until a fix is pushed
A colleague can import the same file in their own browser; that copy is theirs and is just as temporary
units: time: real minutes from the start of the lesson
playback: every step gets the same 1.7 s on screen, so the short steps can be read; the Gantt timeline shows the real minutes
checkDescription: An import is visible only to the browser that imported it and never touches the repository, CI or the site; a publish is visible to everyone exactly when the tests pass, and only then is it permanent; minutes run back to back, an import is quicker than a green publish, and playback markers are ordered.

learnerPrompts.predict: Switch to Import it and pick A colleague before you play. Will your colleague see the lesson, and what would they need to do to see it?
learnerPrompts.explain: Publishing took about 50 minutes and an import under 10. When is the slow way worth it, and what does a failing test protect the people using the site from?
